messages.subject: point counts
messages.body_plain:
Hei!

I am new to the group and to the software. I would like to get som tips on literature
and contact information to  researchers/wildlife managers who have analysed
point counts data  with Distance sampling.

I have collected data on the Svalbard ptarmigang (Lagopus mutus hyperboreus),
and would like to  get in contact with people who have used the method on similar
species.

Look forward to some good tips!

Best regards  shild Ż. Pedersen
 ------------------------------------------------------------------

 shild Ż. Pedersen

Pb. 4695, Thorshov,

messages.subject: Distance software: appeal for sponsorship
messages.body_plain:
This message is an appeal for funds to support further development of the
Distance software.

Many members of the list use version 3.5 of Distance, which was first
released in October 1998.  Since then we have been working on a new version
with substantially expanded capabilities (see below).  We will be releasing
this new software, Distance 4, in December 2000.  As with previous versions
of the program, we are committed to making it available for free over the
internet.

The development of Distance 4 has been supported by the following people and
organizations, and we take this opportunity to thank them publicly:
-  UK Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council
-  UK Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council
-  US National Marine Fisheries Service (main contact Dr Jeff Laake,
     National Marine Mammal Laboratory)
-  USGS Biological Resources Divison (contacts Dr David Anderson and
     Dr Ken Burnham, Colorado Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit)
-  US National Parks Service (main contact Dr Steven Fancy,
     USNPS Inventory and Monitoring Program)

Funding from these sources has enabled us to develop the new features in
Distance 3.5 and Distance 4, and to provide support for Distance in the form
of the web pages, email list, replies to personal queries and program
updates.  As things stand at present our funding for this project will run
out in December.  Thereafter we will be able to provide only very minimal
support for the program, and will not be able to pursue further program
developments.  We are therefore appealing to users who benefit from the
software to consider whether their organization might be able to sponsor the
program.

Sponsors might prefer to fund a specific aspect of program development (see
below), perhaps one that has special relevance to their own work. In
addition, we hope to find a sponsor willing to fund the core activities of
program maintenance and support, who would then become recognized as the main
sponsor of Distance.  Our aim is to secure sufficient funding to allow one
programmer (preferably Len Thomas, the developer of Distance 3.5 and Distance
4.0) to work on development and support for at least six months per year over
the next three years.

Sponsors would benefit directly from any program developments they enable.
In addition, a sponsorship agreement could include priority access to support
and problem fixes, and free places on our distance sampling training
workshops.

Below, we outline the main features that will be in the December release of
Distance 4, and then some of the features that we hope to find sponsorship to
include in future versions of the program.  We encourage anyone who thinks
they can help to contact us.

 - Steve Buckland, Len Thomas and David Borchers
   University of St Andrews
   st...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk

New features in Distance 4
--------------------------

1. GIS functionality.  This includes entry and import of spatially referenced
data (stored as ESRI shapefiles), display of maps, ability to deal with
projections and geo-coordinate systems and a wide variety of units.

2. Automated design algorithms, including random points; systematic grids
of points; randomly-spaced parallel lines; systematically-spaced parallel
lines; zigzag samplers.

3. Estimation of design coverage probability by location throughout the
study region, estimated by simulation, for design algorithms that do not
provide uniform coverage probability.

4. Inclusion of covariates and factors in models for the detection
function, using either the half-normal or the hazard-rate key.

5. Methodology for analysing double-platform survey data, to allow
estimation of density and abundance when detection on the trackline is
uncertain.

6. A data-entry add-in tool that allows advanced users to produce custom
computer data entry forms.  We will implement one add-in tailored for
entry of data collected under a point transect (variable circular plot)
protocol used by the US National Parks Service.  This will enable observers
to enter their survey data into Distance more easily.

Features we hope to include in future versions of Distance
----------------------------------------------------------

(More details of each of these are available on request.)

1. Additional double-platform, multi-platform and composite distance
sampling/mark-recapture capabilities, to widen the applicability of
distance sampling to more types of population.  Possible extensions to the
initial version of our double-platform software include: (i) inclusion of
point transects as well as line transects; (ii) allowing random effects (ie
mixed models) thereby potentially increasing precision and producing more
stable estimates where random effects are appropriate; (iii) extension to
more than two platforms; (iv) inclusion of cue-based methods (the initial
software will only deal with animal-based surveys); (v) modelling of
measurement and rounding error in distances and other regressors;
(vi) extensions to allow more flexible detection functions (e.g. through
use of generalized additive modelling and/or composite link functions).

2. Spatial line and point transect models, to allow density to be modelled
as a function of location.  This has the additional advantages that
precision is potentially improved when spatial covariates are
modelled; abundance can be estimated for any sub-area of interest; data
from non-random surveys, such as surveys conducted on 'platforms of
opportunity', can potentially yield reliable estimates of abundance; and
researchers can explore what spatial covariates influence animal density.

3. Simulation options to allow users to try different survey designs on
simulated populations, to assess which design is likely to be most
efficient for the population of interest.

4. Further options for integrated estimation, using the Horvitz-Thompson
estimator.

5. Further automated design algorithms, to cater for the needs of
specialist groups of users.

6. Improved diagnostics and exploratory data analysis.  Examples include
detection function plots with real-time changes to bin widths and data
summaries for fields other than the distance field.

7. Further data entry add-ins, as required.

8. Further GIS functionality, such as: ability to enter spatial data
directly on to a map; inclusion of raster images on map; refined printing of
maps; improved renderers for density maps.

9. Incorporation of trend estimation into the Distance package, for use with
monitoring programs.

_________________________________________________________________________
